articles.title: Hammer Attack on Shrine at ITO Yamuna Ghat: Hindu Raksha Dal Member Named in Viral Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shrine at the Yamuna Ghat near ITO in Delhi was vandalised on Wednesday after a man allegedly demolished the structure using a hammer. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media, triggering sharp reactions. The accused seen in the video has been identified as Akash Pandit.

body.html:
A shrine at the Yamuna Ghat near ITO in Delhi was vandalised on Wednesday after a man allegedly demolished the structure using a hammer. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media, triggering sharp reactions.

The accused seen in the video has been identified as Akash Pandit. Several social media posts have claimed that he is associated with the Hindu Raksha Dal. In the footage, Akash Pandit and a few others are allegedly seen striking a mazar (tomb-shrine) with hammers, causing visible damage to the structure.

According to claims made by the group, the action was carried out to remove what they described as an “illegal encroachment” and to “free” a temple area from unauthorised occupation. However, there has been no official confirmation from civic or police authorities regarding the legal status of the structure.

The incident comes amid heightened sensitivity around religious structures in the national capital. Earlier, on January 7, 2026, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) carried out a separate court-ordered demolition drive near the Faiz-e-Elahi Masjid at Turkman Gate, clearing around 39,000 square feet of encroached land. That operation involved heavy deployment of police and paramilitary forces due to tensions and incidents of stone-pelting.

In contrast, the incident at the Yamuna Ghat appears to be a localised act allegedly carried out by private individuals. Delhi Police have not yet issued a detailed public statement on the Yamuna Ghat vandalism, and it is not clear whether any formal complaint or case has been registered.

Authorities are expected to examine the viral video and take appropriate action as per law.

articles.title: Parking Row Turns Ugly in Greater Noida West, Viral Video Leads to Arrests
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A case of bullying and verbal abuse following a parking dispute has surfaced from a residential society in Greater Noida West, with a video of the incident going viral on social media. Acting on the victim’s complaint and the viral footage, police have arrested two accused.

body.html:
A case of bullying and verbal abuse following a parking dispute has surfaced from a residential society in Greater Noida West, with a video of the incident going viral on social media. Acting on the victim’s complaint and the viral footage, police have arrested two accused.

The incident took place on January 13, 2026, at First Avenue Society, Gaur City-1, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Bisrakh police station. According to police, an argument broke out over parking between Sushant Gupta, the car driver Guddu Kumar, and the car owner Ayush. What began as a routine dispute soon escalated into verbal abuse and alleged bullying.

Police said Sushant Gupta was subjected to abusive language and threats during the altercation. He recorded the entire episode on his mobile phone, and the video was later circulated widely on social media, triggering public outrage.

After the video went viral, the Bisrakh police took cognisance of the matter and initiated an investigation. Based on the complaint and video evidence, police arrested driver Guddu Kumar, a resident of Pisawa in Aligarh, and car owner Ayush, a resident of First Avenue, Gaur City.

Bisrakh police confirmed that further legal action is underway in the case.

articles.title: Why Bushra Raza Ali Khan is Trending: From Housing Discrimination to a Call for Harmony
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A viral video from Lucknow has sparked a fresh debate on discrimination and social harmony. Bushra Raza Ali Khan, who recently made headlines after claiming a Hindu landlord refused her a flat because of her religion, is trending again.

body.html:
A viral video from Lucknow has sparked a fresh debate on discrimination and social harmony. Bushra Raza Ali Khan, who recently made headlines after claiming a Hindu landlord refused her a flat because of her religion, is trending again.

In her latest video, Bushra makes a powerful appeal to her own community. She urges people to stay away from violence, extremism, and acts that harm society, arguing that such incidents create a climate of fear and lead to discrimination against innocent Muslims in housing, jobs, and daily life.

"Because of the actions of a few, the entire community suffers," she claims, explaining why many landlords and brokers hesitate to rent to Muslims.

The video has ignited a firestorm on social media. While many praise her for her courage and call for peace, others are critical, viewing the video through a political lens. Is this a necessary call for reform, or a symptom of a deeply polarized society?

In this video, we cover:
The background of the Lucknow flat rental controversy.
Bushra Raza Ali Khan’s message to her community.
The social media reaction and the debate on Islamophobia vs. reform.
Impact of extremism on ordinary citizens' lives.

articles.title: ‘Honour’ Killing Shock in Bhind: Father Shoots Dead Married Daughter Over Love Affair
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident was reported from Khiriya Thapak village under the Mehgaon police station area of Bhind district, Madhya Pradesh, where a man allegedly shot dead his own married daughter, citing social shame over her love affair.

body.html:
A shocking incident was reported from Khiriya Thapak village under the Mehgaon police station area of Bhind district, Madhya Pradesh, where a man allegedly shot dead his own married daughter, citing social shame over her love affair. The incident occurred on Tuesday night and came to light on Wednesday morning, sending shockwaves through the village.

According to police, the accused, Munnesh Dhanuk, was angry over his 21-year-old daughter Nidhi Dhanuk’s relationship with another man and her alleged decision to leave home earlier. Police said Munnesh believed her actions had brought social disrepute to the family.

Investigations revealed that Munnesh allegedly lured Nidhi back to the village on Tuesday evening. Later that night, he took her to a mustard field on the outskirts of the village, where he shot her in the chest with a country-made pistol. Nidhi died on the spot.

The incident came to light after Nidhi’s mother, Pooja, informed the police. On Wednesday morning, police reached the spot and recovered the body from the field. The body was sent to Mehgaon Hospital for post-mortem examination. The accused father has been taken into custody and is being interrogated.

Police said Nidhi was married to Devu Dhanuk, a resident of Gudagudi Ka Naka in Gwalior, on December 11. On December 28, she had gone shopping with her husband at Maharaj Bada in Gwalior. During that time, she allegedly disappeared when her husband went to fetch water, prompting both families to search for her.

Villagers claimed that Nidhi was in a relationship with a man from the same village, who was related to her as an uncle. Reports further suggest that after going missing, Nidhi appeared before the Gwalior Kotwali police and stated that she was an adult and had left of her own free will.

Mehgaon SDOP Sanjay Koccha confirmed that a man has been arrested for shooting his married daughter to death in Khiriya Thapak village. He said the police are investigating all aspects of the case to determine the exact motive behind the murder.

articles.title: Foot-Washed Potatoes Spark Outrage at HBTU Kanpur, Students Boycott Mess Food
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Students of the Sridharacharya Hostel at Harcourt Butler Technical University (HBTU), Kanpur, staged a massive protest on Tuesday after a video showing mess staff cleaning potatoes with their feet went viral on social media.

body.html:
Students of the Sridharacharya Hostel at Harcourt Butler Technical University (HBTU), Kanpur, staged a massive protest on Tuesday after a video showing mess staff cleaning potatoes with their feet went viral on social media. Hundreds of students surrounded the administrative building and marched across the campus, demanding strict action and improved facilities.

Students Gaurav Gupta and Vishal Yadav said that when they reached the mess for breakfast, they witnessed a staff member crushing and cleaning potatoes with his feet. After the video spread online, students refused to eat the food and proceeded to the office of the Dean of Students’ Welfare (DSW) to lodge their protest.

The students further alleged that mess staff frequently consume alcohol, cigarettes and tobacco while preparing food, leading to extremely poor food quality. Slogans were raised against the university administration as student leader Abhijeet Rai, along with members of the Chhatra Sangh Bahalti Morcha, joined the protest.

When DSW Professor C.L. Gehlot asked students to return to their classes, they replied that they had been hungry since morning due to the boycott and could not attend lectures. During an inspection of the hostel, students pointed out serious lapses in security and basic facilities.

Student Madhukar Rai claimed he was injured after a piece of ceiling plaster fell on him while he was sleeping at night. He alleged that despite repeated complaints, the warden failed to inspect the hostel. Students also complained that bathrooms lack doors and that there is a severe shortage of water for bathing and handwashing.

The DSW later ordered the expulsion of the guilty mess staff from the hostel and assured students that their grievances regarding food quality, safety and facilities would be addressed at the earliest.

articles.title: FASTag Dispute Turns Violent: Advocate Beaten, Forced to Apologise at Barabanki Toll Plaza
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: An advocate of the Lucknow High Court was allegedly assaulted by toll plaza staff following a dispute over a FASTag balance at the Gotona (Bara) Toll Plaza on the Lucknow–Sultanpur Highway in Barabanki district, Uttar Pradesh.

body.html:
An advocate of the Lucknow High Court was allegedly assaulted by toll plaza staff following a dispute over a FASTag balance at the Gotona (Bara) Toll Plaza on the Lucknow–Sultanpur Highway in Barabanki district, Uttar Pradesh. The incident occurred on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, and triggered widespread outrage among the legal fraternity.

The victim, Ratnesh Shukla, a resident of Pratapgarh, was on his way to court when an argument broke out with toll workers over a FASTag issue. According to the complaint, toll staff used abusive language, surrounded him, chased him and assaulted him. Viral video clips from the scene show several toll employees forcing the advocate to apologise while continuing to beat him.

Shukla sustained serious injuries in the assault and was taken to a nearby Community Health Centre (CHC) for treatment. Based on his complaint, Haidergarh police registered a case and detained three toll plaza employees for questioning.

The incident led to strong protests by advocates, with hundreds of lawyers staging a demonstration outside the Haidergarh police station. The protest caused significant traffic congestion on the national highway for several hours.

Haidergarh Station House Officer (SHO) Abhimanyu Mall confirmed that legal proceedings have been initiated and efforts are underway to identify and arrest other suspects involved in the assault.

articles.title: Caught Red-Handed in Jhansi Hotel: Lover Hides Under Bed as Husband Walks in With Police
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dramatic incident involving a husband, wife and her alleged lover unfolded in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, after a suspicious husband caught his wife red-handed in a hotel room with another man.

body.html:
A dramatic incident involving a husband, wife and her alleged lover unfolded in Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, after a suspicious husband caught his wife red-handed in a hotel room with another man. The high-voltage scene created chaos inside a hotel near the city bus stand and drew police intervention.

The incident occurred on January 11 at Kama Hotel, located in the Navabad police station area. According to police, the husband had been suspecting his wife’s movements for some time and was tracking her activities. His suspicion turned into confirmation when he found her in a hotel room with another man and immediately alerted the police.

When the husband entered the room along with police personnel, the alleged lover panicked and attempted to hide under the bed to escape. However, the police soon pulled him out. The incident led to loud arguments and commotion in the hotel corridors and room, attracting the attention of hotel staff and guests.

Instead of showing remorse, the wife reportedly reacted aggressively. In front of police and onlookers, she claimed she had not been living with her husband for the past two years and said she was ready to divorce him, stating that he was “dead” to her. Her reaction reportedly left even the police surprised.

The husband told police that he had married the woman about three years ago. Soon after the marriage, disputes began between them. In 2023, the wife had filed a case against him, which was later settled. He said he then moved to her maternal uncle’s house in Sipri Bazaar in an attempt to save the marriage. While relations improved briefly, he alleged that his wife continued to secretly meet her lover.

Navabad police took the husband, wife and the alleged lover into custody and brought them to the police station. Station in-charge Ravi Srivastava said the police have received a complaint from the husband and further legal action is being taken accordingly.

articles.title: Road Fight Exposes Sex Racket in Aligarh, 15 Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A fight between two girls on a public road has led the Aligarh Police to uncover a major organized prostitution network operating within the city. In a swift operation carried out by the Bannadevi Police Station, raids were conducted at Chauhan Complex Skyway Hotel and Maraki Hotel.

body.html:
A fight between two girls on a public road has led the Aligarh Police to uncover a major organized prostitution network operating within the city.

In a swift operation carried out by the Bannadevi Police Station, raids were conducted at Chauhan Complex Skyway Hotel and Maraki Hotel. A total of 15 individuals—8 men and 7 women—were arrested from the premises in objectionable conditions.

🚨 Key Details of the Raid:
Location: Bannadevi Police Station Area, Aligarh (UP).
Hotels Raided: Skyway Hotel & Maraki Hotel.
The Masterminds: The racket was allegedly run by hotel owners Ravindra Singh Anand, Rahul Vashishtha, and Shubham Sharma.
Network: Women were reportedly trafficked from Jharkhand and Delhi.
🔍 Significant Recoveries: The police recovered ₹58,070 in cash, 17 mobile phones, 2 visitor registers, ATM cards, swipe machines, and a Verna car. Notably, 3 Press ID cards were also found, suggesting the accused may have been posing as journalists.
⚖️ Legal Action: FIR No. 33/2026 has been registered under Sections 3, 4, 5, and 7 of the Immoral Trafficking (Prevention) Act.
